why_there_is_no_screenshot: This surface cannot be photographed, and that is a property of the surface rather than of
the harness. Both refusal arms of WoocomProductController::index end in
`redirect()->back()` (:50 for the integration arm, :53+ for the permission arm), so the
browser is sent to WHATEVER PAGE IT CAME FROM. There are no pixels of its own to capture.
The four PNGs that used to sit here under this name were therefore pictures of the surface
driven immediately before it in the same sweep -- /webhook/create -- and were byte-identical
to that surface's own captures. check-distinct-surface-captures.py reported them as a
collision, correctly. They were removed rather than regenerated, because regenerating them
would only photograph a different previous page.
This is the `redirect()->back()` trap PHASE-2.5-DEV-FIXTURE-PERMISSIONS.md already records,
in its most literal form: there it keeps the previous page's legitimate TITLE; here it kept

measurement.method: logged in as the fixture merchant, navigated to a known previous page, then to /woocom_product
measurement.conclusion: the landing page follows the referrer, which is what redirect()->back() does

correction_to_the_previously_recorded_re.was: measured HTTP 200 with an empty body and no <html> element in all four combinations
is_wrong_because: The status is 200 only after the redirect is followed, and the body is a FULL page with an
<html> element -- the previous page's. The earlier reading of 'empty body, no <html>' came
from the sweep recording document.title of a page that had not changed: the previous
surface was /webhook/create, a modal fragment with no <title>, so the title read as ''.
correction_to_the_previously_recorded_re.now: refused before it renders. Two gates, and the first is the one that fires for the fixture.

the_two_gates.first: isAbleTo('Manage Woocommerce Product') -- the fixture merchant does NOT hold it (measured against the fixture's role grants)
the_two_gates.second: settings woocommerce_setting_enabled == 'on' -- the setting row does not exist (measured: absent)
the_two_gates.consequence: even granting the permission would stop at the second gate, which needs a connected WooCommerce store with credentials

disposition: BLOCKED is CORRECT and unchanged. Only the stated reason was wrong, and it is corrected in the coverage matrix. Remediation is unchanged: an owner-provided WooCommerce sandbox credential, or an explicit decision to leave these screens unverified in Phase 2.5.
